title: The influence of BCG vaccine strain on mycobacteria-specific and non-specific immune responses in a prospective cohort of infants in Uganda.
ehr_evidence: Infants from the Entebbe Mother and Baby Study (ISRCTN32849447) who received BCG-Russia, BCG-Bulgaria or BCG-Denmark at birth were analysed; data were collected prospectively via questionnaires during antenatal care, blood/stool biospecimens, ELISA cytokine assays, and clinical examination for BCG scars at 12 months.
summary: In a prospective birth cohort of infants in Entebbe, Uganda, comparison of three BCG vaccine strains (Russia, Bulgaria, Denmark) on mycobacteria-specific and non-specific cytokine immune responses, scarring, adverse events, and mortality at 1 year.
key_findings: BCG-Denmark infants had the highest cytokine responses; IFN-γ GMR for Denmark vs Russia to cCFP was 2.24 (95% CI 1.42-4.00, p<0.001).
BCG scar frequency differed significantly by strain: 52.2% (Russia), 64.1% (Bulgaria), 92.6% (Denmark), p<0.001.
Scarred infants had higher IFN-γ (GMR 1.59, 95% CI 1.21-2.10) and IL-13 (GMR 1.63, 95% CI 1.26-2.10) responses to cCFP than non-scarred infants, but no difference for TT/PHA.
BCG-Denmark had the highest frequency of BCG-related adverse events (1.8% vs 1.0% Bulgaria, 0.3% Russia), p=0.025.
Mortality differences between strain groups were not significant (underpowered); HR for Denmark 1.22 (95% CI 0.42-3.53).
captured_features: IFN-γ, IL-5, IL-13, IL-10 cytokine concentrations (ELISA) to cCFP, Ag85, TT, PHA
Birth weight, lymphocyte count, malaria parasitaemia, HIV status
study_design: Prospective cohort (observational strain comparison within a randomised anthelminthic trial cohort)
population: Infants born at Entebbe Hospital, Uganda (2003-2005), 1341 with immunological results at 12 months
limitations: Infants were not randomised to BCG strain, so confounding by calendar time/seasonal exposures could not be fully accounted for.
Study was underpowered to detect mortality differences.
Single time point at 1 year; no TB outcomes or long-term effects analysed.
